program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

Pass if the relevant candidate is visibly white, or all remaining plausible candidates are visibly white; fail if every plausible candidate is visibly nonwhite; unknown if color is indeterminate or candidate ambiguity changes the answer. Distinguish white surface coloration from glare. This check does not establish source-to-edit correspondence or DVD identity.
expanded_nodes.binding: The edited counterpart of the black DVD requested in the source image. Do not assume that the central printed rectangular item, rather than the dark object farther right, is the source target. Use these locations as candidate locators, not as mandatory preserved positions or shapes.

expanded_nodes.question: Does the relevant edited candidate remain identifiable as a DVD?
expanded_nodes.criteria: Inspect DVD identity independently of whiteness. State which edited candidate is being assessed and the visible features or scene context supporting its identity. Pass if the relevant candidate is identifiable as a DVD; fail only if it is clearly a different kind of object; unknown if identity or candidate selection cannot be established. If multiple candidates remain plausible, report their identities separately and use unknown when selecting among them would change the answer. A circular shape alone is not conclusive, but absence of a readable label is not evidence of lost identity. Do not require preservation of a case, printed cover, exact silhouette, or position.
expanded_nodes.binding: The edited candidate for the original black DVD, considering both the central printed source item and the dark source object farther right without preselecting either. Assess the same candidate described by location in the color evidence; source correspondence is checked separately.

expanded_nodes.question: Can the edited candidate assessed by the endpoint checks be matched to the black DVD requested in the source image?
expanded_nodes.criteria: Inspect both images directly. First identify which source object is supported as the requested black DVD, explicitly considering the central printed rectangular item and the dark object farther right rather than assuming either. Then match that target to the edited candidate using stable scene relationships and surviving object-specific evidence. Pass if source-target identification and correspondence are established; fail if the assessed candidate is demonstrably unrelated to the requested target; unknown if target selection or correspondence remains ambiguous. Changed shape, duplication, shared location, or whiteness alone does not settle correspondence. Report any independently established change or lack of change in the actual source target's color, including whether it remains black. Do not infer no progress merely from an unmatched candidate.
expanded_nodes.binding: The black DVD specified by the instruction, identified from the source image rather than from an assumed central-case locator. Compare it with the edited candidates described in s1 and s2. Their observations are advisory and may be corrected by direct image inspection.

expanded_nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
expanded_nodes.criteria: Judge only transformation of the original black DVD. Return complete only when the evidence establishes a corresponding edited target that is white and remains identifiable as a DVD; endpoint observations must concern that same target. A known correspondence is necessary for completion, but no check's pass alone establishes completion. Return partial when evidence establishes whitening of the original target short of completion, including established whitening with loss of DVD identity. Return absent only when explicit evidence establishes no requested progress, such as the actual target remaining black with no whitening. A nonwhite endpoint can still represent partial progress if comparison establishes whitening. An unrelated white candidate, failed matching, or changed object count alone establishes neither progress nor absence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid observations supply no affirmative fact. They prevent completion when a necessary completion fact remains unresolved, but do not block partial or absent when other explicit evidence independently establishes that outcome. Resolve candidate ambiguity only from supplied matching evidence, never by assuming the central or right-hand candidate is the target. Return unknown when the evidence cannot distinguish complete, partial, and absent.
expanded_nodes.binding: Target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.. Reference: The black DVD in the input image..

transactions.reason: The source contains a printed rectangular DVD-like item near the center, whereas the edit contains white circular objects. This suggests a correspondence ambiguity, not an established absence of progress. Earlier repairs either treated packaging as mandatory or allowed endpoint passes without established correspondence. Assess whiteness on the matched source target, retain a separate DVD-identity observation, and conditionally inspect actual whitening progress when the white endpoint is not established. The construction and audit errors do not establish visual answers, and the reference label must not determine the checks.

actions.question: Is the original black DVD visibly white in the edited image?
actions.criteria: Inspect the edited endpoint's color first, then compare it with the source to establish that the observation concerns the requested DVD. Identify the source target and edited counterpart explicitly. The printed rectangular item near the source center is a plausible locator, not a packaging-preservation requirement. Pass only if the evidence establishes that the requested source DVD has a visibly white edited counterpart. Fail if its established counterpart remains black or is another color. Use unknown if source-target selection, correspondence, or surface color cannot be established. Neither a nearby white circle nor a changed silhouette alone establishes or disproves correspondence. Describe intermediate or mixed coloration when visible.
actions.binding: The black DVD specified in the source image, tracked to its edited counterpart. Distinguish the central printed item from the separate dark object farther right without assuming that either edited white object is the transformed DVD.

actions.question: Does the edited counterpart of the original black DVD remain identifiable as a DVD?
actions.criteria: Inspect both images independently of the color verdict. Identify the source DVD and the edited object being assessed. Pass if correspondence and visible features or scene context support that the counterpart remains a DVD. Fail only if the matched counterpart is visibly a different kind of object. Use unknown if correspondence or identity is ambiguous. Disc shape can contribute evidence but is not automatically sufficient or automatically inadequate. Do not require readable labels, preservation of packaging, an unchanged rectangular silhouette, or a separately resolved DVD-versus-CD distinction unsupported by the images.
actions.binding: The original black DVD and its edited counterpart, not an arbitrary edited white disc. The central printed source item is a candidate locator rather than an immutable shape requirement.

actions.question: Has any visible black-to-white color change progressed on the original DVD?
actions.criteria: Compare the source DVD with its edited counterpart directly, even if earlier observations are unknown. Pass if an established corresponding target shows actual whitening, such as a lighter intermediate surface or some surface changed to white. Fail only if sufficient comparison evidence establishes no requested color progress, such as the original target remaining black without whitening. Use unknown if target selection, correspondence, or the presence of whitening cannot be established. Describe whether any established whitening reaches the white endpoint. An added white object, removal of the target, or edits to a different object do not themselves establish requested progress or its absence.
actions.binding: The requested black DVD in the source image and any reliably corresponding edited target. Inspect its surface-color change, not the number of white objects or preservation of its case.
actions.readout_criteria: Use the observations and their explicit evidence, not a count of passes. Return complete when s1 and s2 pass about the same original target: s1 already establishes correspondence and a white endpoint, and s2 establishes retained DVD identity. In this case s3_whitening_progress may legitimately be skipped because the established white transformation already establishes progress. Return partial when actual whitening is established but completion is demonstrably unmet, including a nonwhite intermediate endpoint or a white counterpart established to have lost DVD identity. Return absent only when explicit comparison evidence establishes no requested whitening of the original target; unresolved identity does not block an otherwise established absence of color progress. A failed white-endpoint check alone does not distinguish partial from absent. Unknown, skipped, or invalid observations establish no visual fact. If progress is known but whether completion is achieved remains genuinely uncertain, return unknown rather than assuming partial. Return unknown whenever the supplied evidence cannot establish complete, partial, or absent. Do not infer an outcome from the reference label or count unrelated edits as progress.
